Work: བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའི་སྤྱོད་པ་ལ་འཇུག་པ།, author: unknown. A canonical Tibetan text; the blocks below are being translated in order.

Preceding blocks of this same document and their translations — match this terminology, register and line shape:

[9-11] source:
སྒྱུ་མའི་སྐྱེས་བུ་བསད་སོགས་ལ། །
སེམས་མེད་ཕྱིར་ན་སྡིག་མེད་དེ། །
སྒྱུ་མའི་སེམས་དང་ལྡན་པ་ལ། །
བསོད་ནམས་དང་ནི་སྡིག་པ་འབྱུང་། །
[9-11] translation already produced for this document:
In killing an illusory person and so forth,
Because there is no mind, there is no sin;
But regarding that which possesses an illusory mind,
Merit and sin arise.

[9-12] source:
སྔགས་སོགས་རྣམས་ལ་ནུས་མེད་ཕྱིར། །
སྒྱུ་མའི་སེམས་ནི་འབྱུང་བ་མེད། །
སྣ་ཚོགས་རྐྱེན་ལས་བྱུང་བ་ཡི། །
སྒྱུ་མ་དེ་ཡང་སྣ་ཚོགས་ཉིད། །
[9-12] translation already produced for this document:
Because mantras and so forth lack the capacity,
Illusory minds do not arise.
Arising from various conditions,
Illusions themselves are also various.

[9-13] source:
རྐྱེན་གཅིག་གིས་ནི་ཀུན་ནུས་པ། །
གང་ན་ཡང་ནི་ཡོད་མ་ཡིན། །
གལ་ཏེ་དོན་དམ་མྱ་ངན་འདས། །
འཁོར་བ་ཀུན་རྫོབ་དེ་ལྟ་ན། །
[9-13] translation already produced for this document:
That a single condition has the capacity for everything
Nowhere exists.
"If the ultimate is nirvāṇa,
And saṃsāra is the relative, in that case,

[9-14] source:
སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱང་ནི་འཁོར་འགྱུར་བས། །
བྱང་ཆུབ་སྤྱོད་པས་ཅི་ཞིག་བྱ། །
རྐྱེན་རྣམས་རྒྱུན་ནི་མ་ཆད་ན། །
སྒྱུ་མའང་ལྡོག་པར་མི་འགྱུར་གྱི། །
[9-14] translation already produced for this document:
Even a Buddha would cycle in saṃsāra, so
What is the point of bodhisattva conduct?"
If the continuum of conditions is not severed,
Even an illusion is not reversed;

[9-15] source:
རྐྱེན་རྣམས་རྒྱུན་ནི་ཆད་པས་ན། །
ཀུན་རྫོབ་ཏུ་ཡང་མི་འབྱུང་ངོ་། །
གང་ཚེ་འཁྲུལ་པའང་ཡོད་མིན་ན། །
སྒྱུ་མ་གང་གིས་དམིགས་པར་འགྱུར། །
[9-15] translation already produced for this document:
But because the continuum of conditions is severed,
It does not arise even relatively.
"When even the deceptive mind does not exist,
By what is the illusion perceived?"

[9-16] source:
གང་ཚེ་ཁྱོད་ལ་སྒྱུ་མ་ཉིད། །
མེད་ནའང་དེ་ཚེ་ཅི་ཞིག་དམིགས། །
གལ་ཏེ་དེ་ཉིད་དུ་གཞན་ཡོད། །
རྣམ་པ་དེ་ནི་སེམས་ཉིད་ཡིན། །
[9-16] translation already produced for this document:
When, for you, even the illusion itself
Does not exist, then what is perceived?
"If it exists as another in reality,
That aspect is the mind itself."

heading: ལེའུ་དགུ་པ། ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ།
translation:
If it is not seen by anyone at all,
Whether it is luminous or not luminous,
Like the alluring pose of a barren woman's daughter,
Expressing it is meaningless.

translation:
"If self-awareness does not exist,
How is consciousness remembered?"
It is remembered from its connection to experiencing another,
Like the poison of a rat.

translation:
"Endowed with other conditions,
Because it sees, it illuminates itself."
Through the application of accomplished eye-ointment,
A vase is seen, but not the eye-ointment itself.

In killing an illusory person and so forth,
Because there is no mind, there is no sin;
But regarding that which possesses an illusory mind,
Merit and sin arise.

སྔགས་སོགས་རྣམས་ལ་ནུས་མེད་ཕྱིར། །

[9-12] translation already produced for this document:
Because mantras and so forth lack the capacity,
Illusory minds do not arise.
Arising from various conditions,
Illusions themselves are also various.

[9-13] source:
རྐྱེན་གཅིག་གིས་ནི་ཀུན་ནུས་པ། །

[9-13] translation already produced for this document:

Nowhere exists.

And saṃsāra is the relative, in that case,

བྱང་ཆུབ་སྤྱོད་པས་ཅི་ཞིག་བྱ། །

Even a Buddha would cycle in saṃsāra, so
What is the point of bodhisattva conduct?"
If the continuum of conditions is not severed,
Even an illusion is not reversed;

རྐྱེན་རྣམས་རྒྱུན་ནི་ཆད་པས་ན། །

But because the continuum of conditions is severed,
It does not arise even relatively.

By what is the illusion perceived?"

གང་ཚེ་ཁྱོད་ལ་སྒྱུ་མ་ཉིད། །

Does not exist, then what is perceived?

That aspect is the mind itself."

translation:
How things are seen, heard, and known
Is not to be refuted here;
Here, what becomes the cause of suffering,
The conceptualization of true existence, is to be reversed.

And if it is not conceived as being not other,"

translation:

How can there be a result?"
Because whether he remains or has passed into nirvāṇa,
It is taught that it is exactly the same.

translation:

What is the use of seeing emptiness?"
Because scriptures state that without this path,
There is no awakening.

གཅིག་པུ་ཉིད་དུ་འགྱུར་བ་ཡིན། །
[9-28] translation already produced for this document:
"Since a non-entity depends on a real entity,
How could it be endowed with a function?"
Your mind, being without a companion,
Would become entirely alone.

[9-29] source:
གང་ཚེ་སེམས་ནི་གཟུང་བྲལ་བ། །
དེ་ཚེ་ཐམས་ཅད་དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས། །
དེ་ལྟ་ན་ཡང་སེམས་ཙམ་དུ། །
བརྟགས་ལ་ཡོན་ཏན་ཅི་ཞིག་ཡོད། །
[9-29] translation already produced for this document:
When the mind is free of an apprehended object,
At that time, all are Tathāgatas.
Even in that case, in Mind Only,
What merit is there in conceptualizing it?

[9-30] source:
སྒྱུ་མ་ལྟ་བུར་ཤེས་ན་ཡང་། །
ཇི་ལྟར་ཉོན་མོངས་ལྡོག་འགྱུར་ཏེ། །
གང་ཚེ་སྒྱུ་མའི་བུད་མེད་ལ། །
དེ་བྱེད་ཉིད་ཀྱང་ཆགས་སྐྱེ་འགྱུར། །
[9-30] translation already produced for this document:
Even if one knows things to be like an illusion,
How are the afflictions repelled?
Since, toward an illusory woman,
Even her creator generates attachment.

[9-31] source:
དེ་བྱེད་པ་ནི་ཤེས་བྱ་ལ། །
ཉོན་མོངས་བག་ཆགས་མ་སྤངས་པ། །
དེས་ན་དེ་མཐོང་བ་ན་དེ། །
སྟོང་ཉིད་བག་ཆགས་ཉམ་ཆུང་ཉིད། །
[9-31] translation already produced for this document:
Her creator has not abandoned
The latent tendencies of the afflictions toward objects of knowledge;
Therefore, when he sees her,
His latent tendencies for emptiness are weak.

[9-32] source:
སྟོང་ཉིད་བག་ཆགས་གོམས་པས་ནི། །
དངོས་པོའི་བག་ཆགས་སྤོང་འགྱུར་ཞིང་། །
ཅི་ཡང་མེད་ཅེས་གོམས་པས་ནི། །
དེ་ཡང་ཕྱི་ནས་སྤོང་བར་འགྱུར། །
[9-32] translation already produced for this document:
By familiarizing with the latent tendencies of emptiness,
The latent tendencies of entities will be abandoned;
By familiarizing with "there is nothing at all,"
That too will later be abandoned.

heading: ལེའུ་དགུ་པ། ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ།
translation:
"If the Mahāyāna is not established,
How is your scripture established?"
"Because this is established for both of us."
"Initially, this was not established for you."

དཔེར་ན་ནམ་མཁའ་ལྡིང་གི་ནི། །

It pacifies poison and so forth.

Into nirvāṇa, he accomplishes all aims.

སེམས་མེད་པ་ལ་མཆོད་བྱས་པས། །

གང་ཕྱིར་བཞུགས་པའམ་མྱ་ངན་འདས། །

How can there be a result?"
Because whether he remains or has passed into nirvāṇa,
It is taught that it is exactly the same.

[9-39] source:
ཀུན་རྫོབ་བམ་ནི་དེ་ཉིད་དུའང་། །

[9-39] translation already produced for this document:
Whether conventionally or in reality,
It is suitable, for scriptures state that there is a result;
For example, toward a true Buddha,
Just as it is endowed with a result.

[9-40] source:
བདེན་པ་མཐོང་བས་གྲོལ་འགྱུར་གྱི། །
སྟོང་ཉིད་མཐོང་བས་ཅི་ཞིག་བྱ། །
གང་ཕྱིར་ལུང་ལས་ལམ་འདི་ནི། །
མེད་པར་བྱང་ཆུབ་མེད་པར་གསུངས། །
[9-40] translation already produced for this document:
"One is liberated by seeing the truths;
What is the use of seeing emptiness?"
Because scriptures state that without this path,
There is no awakening.

That is the same for the Mahāyāna too.

The Vedas and so forth would also become true.

If you say the Mahāyāna is subject to dispute,
The scriptures are disputed by non-Buddhists,
And other scriptures are disputed by ourselves and others;
Since they are subject to dispute, they would have to be discarded.

How can fear arise toward it?

Work: བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའི་སྤྱོད་པ་ལ་འཇུག་པ།, author: unknown. A canonical Tibetan text; the blocks below are being translated in order.

Preceding blocks of this same document and their translations — match this terminology, register and line shape:

[9-43] source:
ཐེག་ཆེན་རྩོད་བཅས་ཕྱིར་ཞེ་ན། །
ལུང་ལ་མུ་སྟེགས་པ་རྣམས་དང་། །
ལུང་གཞན་ལ་ཡང་རང་གཞན་དག །
རྩོད་བཅས་ཡིན་ཕྱིར་དོར་བྱར་འགྱུར། །
[9-43] translation already produced for this document:
If you say the Mahāyāna is subject to dispute,
The scriptures are disputed by non-Buddhists,
And other scriptures are disputed by ourselves and others;
Since they are subject to dispute, they would have to be discarded.

[9-44] source:
བསྟན་རྩ་དགེ་སློང་ཉིད་ཡིན་ན། །
དགེ་སློང་ཉིད་ཀྱང་དཀའ་བར་གནས། །
སེམས་ནི་དམིགས་དང་བཅས་རྣམས་ཀྱི། །
མྱ་ངན་འདས་པའང་དཀའ་བར་གནས། །
[9-44] translation already produced for this document:
If being a monk is the root of the teaching,
Even being a monk is difficult to establish.
For those whose minds have apprehension,
Even nirvāṇa is difficult to establish.

[9-45] source:
ཉོན་མོངས་སྤངས་པས་གྲོལ་ན་དེའི། །
དེ་མ་ཐག་ཏུ་དེར་འགྱུར་རོ། །
ཉོན་མོངས་མེད་ཀྱང་དེ་དག་ལ། །
ལས་ཀྱི་ནུས་པ་མཐོང་བ་ཡིན། །
[9-45] translation already produced for this document:
If one is liberated by abandoning afflictions,
It would occur immediately upon that.
Even though there are no afflictions, in them
The power of karma is seen.

[9-46] source:
རེ་ཞིག་ཉེར་ལེན་སྲེད་པ་ནི། །
མེད་ཅེས་ངེས་པ་ཉིད་ཅེ་ན། །
སྲེད་དེ་ཉོན་མོངས་ཅན་མིན་ཡང་། །
ཀུན་རྨོངས་བཞིན་དུ་ཅི་སྟེ་མེད། །
[9-46] translation already produced for this document:
As for the craving for appropriation,
If you say it is certain that it does not exist;
Even if that craving is not an affliction,
Why would it not exist, like ignorance?

[9-47] source:
ཚོར་བའི་རྐྱེན་གྱིས་སྲེད་པ་ཡིན། །
ཚོར་བ་དེ་དག་ལ་ཡང་ཡོད། །
དམིགས་པ་དང་ནི་བཅས་པའི་སེམས། །
འགའ་ཞིག་ལ་ནི་གནས་པར་འགྱུར། །
[9-47] translation already produced for this document:
Craving occurs due to the condition of feeling;
Those ones also have feelings.
A mind that is endowed with apprehension
Will rest upon something.

[9-48] source:
སྟོང་ཉིད་དང་ནི་བྲལ་བའི་སེམས། །
འགགས་པ་སླར་ཡང་སྐྱེ་འགྱུར་ཏེ། །
འདུ་ཤེས་མེད་པའི་སྙོམས་འཇུག་བཞིན། །
དེས་ན་སྟོང་ཉིད་བསྒོམ་པར་བྱ། །
[9-48] translation already produced for this document:
A mind separated from emptiness,
Though ceased, will arise again,
Like the meditative absorption without discrimination;
Therefore, one should meditate on emptiness.

heading: ལེའུ་དགུ་པ། ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ།
translation:
Teeth, hair, and nails are not the self;
The self is not bone or blood.
It is not snot, nor is it phlegm,
And it is neither serum nor pus.

[9-51] source:
ངག་གང་འོད་སྲུངས་ཆེན་པོ་ལ། །
སོགས་པས་གཏིང་དཔོགས་མ་གྱུར་པ། །
དེ་ནི་ཁྱོད་ཀྱིས་མ་རྟོགས་པས། །
གཟུང་བྱ་མིན་པར་སུ་ཞིག་བྱེད། །
[9-51] translation already produced for this document:
Any speech whose depth was unfathomed
By Mahākāśyapa and the rest,
Just because you do not understand it,
Who would make it unacceptable?

[9-52] source:
རྨོངས་པས་སྡུག་བསྔལ་ཅན་དོན་དུ། །
ཆགས་དང་འཇིགས་མཐའ་ལས་གྲོལ་བ། །
འཁོར་བར་གནས་པ་གྲུབ་འགྱུར་བ། །
འདི་ནི་སྟོང་ཉིད་འབྲས་བུ་ཡིན། །
[9-52] translation already produced for this document:
For the sake of those who suffer due to ignorance,
Being freed from the extremes of attachment and fear,
Remaining in saṃsāra becomes established;
This is the result of emptiness.

[9-53] source:
དེ་ལྟར་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་ཕྱོགས་ལ། །
སུན་འབྱིན་པ་ནི་འཐད་མ་ཡིན། །
དེས་ན་ཐེ་ཚོམ་མི་ཟ་བར། །
སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་ནི་བསྒོམ་པར་བྱ། །
[9-53] translation already produced for this document:
Thus, toward the side of emptiness,
Refutation is not appropriate.
Therefore, without hesitation,
One should meditate on emptiness.

[9-54] source:
ཉོན་མོངས་ཤེས་བྱའི་སྒྲིབ་པ་ཡི། །
མུན་པའི་གཉེན་པོ་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད། །
མྱུར་དུ་ཐམས་ཅད་མཁྱེན་འདོད་པས། །
དེ་ནི་ཇི་ལྟར་སྒོམ་མི་བྱེད། །
[9-54] translation already produced for this document:
Of the obscurations of afflictions and knowables,
Emptiness is the antidote to the darkness.
By one who wishes to quickly become omniscient,
How could one not meditate on it?

[9-55] source:
དངོས་གང་སྡུག་བསྔལ་སྐྱེད་བྱེད་པ། །
དེ་ལས་སྐྲག་པ་སྐྱེ་འགྱུར་ན། །
སྟོང་ཉིད་སྡུག་བསྔལ་ཞི་བྱེད་པ། །
དེ་ལ་འཇིགས་པ་ཇི་ལྟར་སྐྱེ། །
[9-55] translation already produced for this document:
Whatever entity produces suffering,
From that, fear will arise.
Since emptiness pacifies suffering,
How can fear arise toward it?

[9-56] source:
གལ་ཏེ་བདག་འགའ་ཡོད་ན་ནི། །
ཅི་ཡང་རུང་ལས་འཇིགས་འགྱུར་ན། །
བདག་ཉིད་འགའ་ཡང་ཡོད་མིན་པས། །
འཇིགས་པར་འགྱུར་བ་སུ་ཞིག་ཡིན། །
[9-56] translation already produced for this document:
If any self existed,
Fear would arise from anything.
Since no self exists at all,
Who is there to be afraid?

heading: ལེའུ་དགུ་པ། ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ།
translation:
The self is not fat or sweat,
And lungs and liver are not the self.
The other internal organs are also not the self,
And the self is not feces or urine.

translation:
Flesh and skin are not the self,
And warmth and wind are not the self.
The cavities are not the self, and in all ways
The six consciousnesses are not the self either.

It would logically follow that wood is also consciousness.
Therefore, it is certain that without a nearby
Object of knowledge, there is no consciousness.

If the self does not exist,
The connection between actions and results is not logical,
Because if one perishes after performing an action,
Whose action will it be?

That there is no self operating there,

That an agent and an experiencer are taught.

མེད་པར་ཤེས་པ་མེད་ཅེས་ངེས། །
[9-61] translation already produced for this document:
If there is consciousness without cognizing,
It would logically follow that wood is also consciousness.
Therefore, it is certain that without a nearby
Object of knowledge, there is no consciousness.

[9-62] source:
དེ་ཉིད་ཀྱིས་ནི་གཟུགས་ཤེས་ན། །
དེ་ཚེ་ཐོས་པའང་ཅི་སྟེ་མིན། །
གལ་ཏེ་སྒྲ་མི་ཉེ་ཕྱིར་ན། །
དེས་ན་དེ་ཡི་ཤེས་པའང་མེད། །
[9-62] translation already produced for this document:
If that very same consciousness cognizes form,
Why is there no hearing at that time?
If it is because sound is not nearby,
Then the consciousness of it is also non-existent.

[9-63] source:
སྒྲ་འཛིན་རང་བཞིན་གང་ཡིན་པ། །
དེ་གཟུགས་འཛིན་པར་ཇི་ལྟར་འགྱུར། །
གཅིག་ནི་ཕ་དང་བུ་ཉིད་དུ། །
བརྟགས་ཡིན་ཡང་དག་ཉིད་མིན་ཏེ། །
[9-63] translation already produced for this document:
How could that which has the nature of apprehending sound
Become the apprehender of form?
One being both father and son
Is designated, but it is not ultimate reality.

[9-64] source:
འདི་ལྟར་སྙིང་སྟོབས་རྡུལ་དང་ནི། །
མུན་པ་བུ་མིན་ཕ་ཡང་མིན། །
དེ་ནི་སྒྲ་འཛིན་དང་ལྡན་པའི། །
རང་བཞིན་དུ་ནི་མཐོང་མ་ཡིན། །
[9-64] translation already produced for this document:
Thus, sattva, rajas, and
Tamas are neither son nor father;
And it is not seen to have a nature
Possessing the apprehension of sound.

heading: ལེའུ་དགུ་པ། ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ།
translation:
The mind of the past and the future
Is not the self, because it does not exist.
But if the arisen mind is the self,
When that perishes, there is no self either.

Conscious and unconscious things, too,
Would become one, because their existence is the same.
When differences are false,
What then is the basis for similarity?

སེམས་མེད་པ་ཡང་བདག་མིན་ཏེ། །

[9-68] translation already produced for this document:
The unconscious is not the self either,
Because it is unconscious, like a vase and so forth.
However, if you say it cognizes because it possesses consciousness,
When it cognizes, it logically follows that the unconscious perishes.

ཇི་སྟེ་བདག་ལ་འགྱུར་མེད་ན། །

[9-69] translation already produced for this document:
But if the self has no change,
What is done to it by consciousness?
Thus, unconscious and devoid of activity,
Space might as well be made into the self.

[9-70] source:
གལ་ཏེ་བདག་ནི་ཡོད་མིན་ན། །

[9-70] translation already produced for this document:
If the self does not exist,
The connection between actions and results is not logical,
Because if one perishes after performing an action,
Whose action will it be?

[9-71] source:
བྱ་བ་འབྲས་གཞི་ཐ་དད་དང་། །
དེར་བདག་བྱེད་པ་མེད་པར་ཡང་། །
ཡུ་བུ་གཉི་ག་ལ་གྲུབ་པས། །

[9-71] translation already produced for this document:
That the bases of the action and the result are different, and
That there is no self operating there,
Is established for both of us, so
Is it not pointless to debate here?

[9-72] source:
རྒྱུ་ལྡན་འབྲས་བུ་དང་བཅས་ཞེས། །
མཐོང་བ་འདི་ནི་སྲིད་མ་ཡིན། །
རྒྱུད་གཅིག་ལ་ནི་བརྟེན་ནས་སུ། །
བྱེད་པོ་སྤྱོད་པོ་ཞེས་བྱར་བསྟན། །
[9-72] translation already produced for this document:
That the one possessing the cause also possesses the result—
To see this is impossible.
It is in dependence upon a single continuum
That an agent and an experiencer are taught.

translation:
For example, the trunk of a banana tree,
When divided into parts, is nothing at all;
Likewise, when analytically
Searched for, the self is also not real.

If sentient beings do not exist,
Toward whom does one practice compassion?
Toward whatever is imputed by the delusion
That is accepted for the sake of the result.

Increases because of the delusion of a self.

Meditating on selflessness is the best.

The body is not the feet or the calves,
The thighs and the waist are also not the body.
The belly and the back are not the body,
And the chest and the arms are not the body.

The body appears like a person.
Likewise, as long as it is present in the hands and so forth,
For that long, the body appears there.

སྡུག་བསྔལ་རྒྱུ་ཡི་ང་རྒྱལ་ནི། །
བདག་ཏུ་རྨོངས་པས་འཕེལ་བར་འགྱུར། །
དེ་ལས་ཀྱང་བཟློག་མེད་ཅེ་ན། །
བདག་མེད་བསྒོམ་པ་མཆོག་ཡིན་ནོ། །
[9-77] translation already produced for this document:
Pride, which is the cause of suffering,
Increases because of the delusion of a self.
If you say, "Even that cannot be reversed,"
Meditating on selflessness is the best.

[9-78] source:
ལུས་ནི་རྐང་པ་བྱིན་པ་མིན། །
བརླ་དང་རྐེད་པའང་ལུས་མ་ཡིན། །
ལྟོ་དང་རྒྱབ་ཀྱང་ལུས་མིན་ཏེ། །
བྲང་དང་དཔུང་པའང་ལུས་མ་ཡིན། །
[9-78] translation already produced for this document:
The body is not the feet or the calves,
The thighs and the waist are also not the body.
The belly and the back are not the body,
And the chest and the arms are not the body.

[9-79] source:
རྩིབ་ལོགས་ལག་པའང་ལུས་མིན་ཏེ། །
མཆན་ཁུང་ཕྲག་པའང་ལུས་མ་ཡིན། །
ནང་ཁྲོལ་རྣམས་ཀྱང་དེ་མིན་ལ། །
མགོ་དང་མགྲིན་པའང་ལུས་མིན་ན། །
འདི་ལ་ལུས་ནི་གང་ཞིག་ཡིན། །
[9-79] translation already produced for this document:
The ribs and the hands are not the body,
The armpits and the shoulders are not the body.
The inner organs are also not it,
And the head and the neck are not the body;
What is the body in all this?

[9-80] source:
གལ་ཏེ་ལུས་འདི་ཐམས་ཅད་ལ། །
ཕྱོགས་རེ་ཡིས་ནི་གནས་གྱུར་ན། །
ཆ་རྣམས་ཆ་ལ་གནས་གྱུར་མོད། །
དེ་རང་ཉིད་ནི་གང་ལ་གནས། །
[9-80] translation already produced for this document:
If this body were to abide in all of these
In a partial manner,
The parts would indeed abide in the parts,
But where does it itself abide?

heading: ལེའུ་དགུ་པ། ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ།
translation:
If it is because it is overshadowed by something stronger
That it is not experienced,
How can that which is not of the nature of experience
Be a feeling?

ཕྱོགས་དབྱེའང་ཆ་ཤས་དང་བྲལ་ཕྱིར། །
མཁའ་བཞིན་དེས་ན་རྡུལ་ཡང་མེད། །

It is like space; therefore, even particles do not exist.

དེ་ཚེ་སྐྱེས་གང་བུད་མེད་གང་། །
[9-87] translation already produced for this document:
Thus, what intelligent person would be attached
To form, which is like a dream?
When the body does not exist in that way,
Then what is a man and what is a woman?

[9-88] source:
སྡུག་བསྔལ་དེ་ཉིད་དུ་ཡོད་ན། །
ཅི་སྟེ་རབ་དགའ་ལ་མི་གནོད། །
བདེ་ན་མྱ་ངན་གདུང་སོགས་ལ། །

[9-88] translation already produced for this document:
If suffering truly existed,
Why does it not harm the very joyful?
If happiness [truly existed], for those overcome with grief and so forth,
Why do delicious foods and so forth not cause joy?

heading: ལེའུ་དགུ་པ། ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ།
translation:
"Suffering exists in a subtle state;
Has its gross state not been removed?"
If you say, "That is merely a joy distinct from that,"
Then that subtle state too is [a state] of that [joy].

Is it not established that the conception of feeling

Where would they meet?
Even if there is no gap, they are a single entity,

Without entering, there is no mixing,
And without mixing, there is no meeting.

The mind does not abide in the sense faculties,
Nor in forms and so forth, nor in between them.

And it is not found anywhere else.

བར་མེད་ན་ཡང་གཅིག་ཉིད་དེ། །
གང་ཞིག་གང་དང་ཕྲད་པར་འགྱུར། །
[9-93] translation already produced for this document:
If there is a gap between the sense faculties and objects,
Where would they meet?
Even if there is no gap, they are a single entity,
So what would meet with what?

[9-94] source:
རྡུལ་ཕྲན་རྡུལ་ཕྲན་ལ་འཇུག་མེད། །
དེ་ནི་སྐབས་མེད་མཉམ་པ་ཡིན། །
མ་ཞུགས་པ་ལ་འདྲེས་མེད་ཅིང་། །
མ་འདྲེས་པ་ལ་ཕྲད་པ་མེད། །
[9-94] translation already produced for this document:
An atom does not enter an atom,
For they have no empty space and are of equal size.
Without entering, there is no mixing,
And without mixing, there is no meeting.

[9-95] source:
ཆ་མེད་པ་ལའང་ཕྲད་པ་ཞེས། །
བྱ་བ་ཇི་ལྟར་འཐད་པར་འགྱུར། །
ཕྲད་པ་དང་ནི་ཆ་མེད་པར། །
གལ་ཏེ་མཐོང་ན་བསྟན་པར་གྱིས། །
[9-95] translation already produced for this document:
How could it be reasonable to say
That what is partless can meet?
If meeting and being partless
Have been seen together, show it!

ཚོགས་པའང་དངོས་པོ་མེད་ཕྱིར་ཏེ། །
སྔར་ནི་ཇི་ལྟར་རྣམ་དཔྱད་བཞིན། །
[9-96] translation already produced for this document:
For consciousness, which has no body,
Meeting is not reasonable at all.
Neither is it for an aggregation, because it does not exist as a real entity,
Just as was analytically examined before.

heading: ལེའུ་དགུ་པ། ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ།
translation:
Or if it exists after the object of knowledge,
Then from what does consciousness arise?
In this way, of all phenomena,
Arising cannot be realized.

How could the two truths exist in that?
And if that is due to another conventional reality,
How could sentient beings pass into nirvāṇa?

From the variations of prior causes themselves.
Why are causes able to produce effects?
From the power of prior causes themselves.

If Īśvara is the cause of beings,
Tell me, for now, what is Īśvara?
If one says it is the elements, so be it;
But what is the use of exhausting oneself over a mere name?

དེ་ཉིད་ཤིན་ཏུ་དཀའ་བར་གནས། །
གལ་ཏེ་ཤེས་དབང་ལས་དོན་གྲུབ། །
ཤེས་ཡོད་ཉིད་ལ་རྟེན་ཅི་ཡོད། །
[9-111] translation already produced for this document:
According to those who hold these two to be true,
That very position rests in great difficulty.
If the object is established by the power of consciousness,
What is the basis for the existence of consciousness itself?

[9-112] source:
འོན་ཏེ་ཤེས་བྱ་ལས་ཤེས་གྲུབ། །
ཤེས་བྱ་ཡོད་ལ་རྟེན་ཅི་ཡོད། །
དེ་སྟེ་ཕན་ཚུན་དབང་གིས་ཡོད། །
གཉི་ག་ཡང་ནི་མེད་པར་འགྱུར། །
[9-112] translation already produced for this document:
Or if consciousness is established from the object of knowledge,
What is the basis for the existence of the object of knowledge?
If they exist by the power of one another,
Both also would not exist.

heading: ལེའུ་དགུ་པ། ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ།
translation:
And what is it that he wishes to produce?
Are not the self, those such as earth,
And the essence of Īśvara permanent?
Consciousness arises from the object of knowledge, and

Īśvara is not space, because it is devoid of movement;
He is not the self, because it was already refuted before;

What is the use of speaking of the inconceivable?

Tell me, what was produced by him?
If the cause has no beginning,
How can the effect have a beginning?

Would be the cause, and not Īśvara.
When assembled, there is no power not to produce,
And without them, there is no power to produce.

གལ་ཏེ་དབང་ཕྱུག་མི་འདོད་བཞིན། །

The qualities known as Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas,
Abiding in equilibrium,
Are termed Pradhāna;
In disequilibrium, they are said to be beings.

[9-128] source:
གཅིག་ལ་རང་བཞིན་གསུམ་ཉིད་ནི། །

[9-128] translation already produced for this document:
For one thing to have three natures
Is illogical, therefore it does not exist.
Likewise, the qualities do not exist,
Because they too would each have three aspects.

heading: ལེའུ་དགུ་པ། ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ།
translation:
Pleasure and so forth are from cloth and so forth;
Since they do not exist, pleasure and so forth do not exist.
Moreover, permanent pleasure and so forth
Are never observed.

If the manifestation of pleasure and so forth exists,
Why is the experience not apprehended?
If that itself becomes subtle,
How can it be both coarse and subtle?

That coarseness and subtlety are impermanent.
Likewise, why do you not assert
That all things are impermanent?

[9-125] translation already produced for this document:
If Īśvara creates without desiring it,
It follows that he is under the control of another.
Even if he desires, he is dependent upon desire.
If he creates, how is he Īśvara?

[9-126] source:
གང་དག་རྡུལ་ཕྲན་རྟག་སྨྲ་བ། །

[9-126] translation already produced for this document:
As for those who assert permanent atoms,
They have also already been refuted earlier.
The permanent Pradhāna is the cause of beings;
This is what the Sāṃkhyas assert.

སྙིང་སྟོབས་རྡུལ་དང་མུན་པ་ཞེས། །
བྱ་བའི་ཡོན་ཏན་མཉམ་གནས་ནི། །
གཙོ་བོ་ཞེས་བྱར་རབ་བརྗོད་དེ། །
མི་མཉམ་འགྲོ་བ་ཡིན་པར་བརྗོད། །
[9-127] translation already produced for this document:
The qualities known as Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas,
Abiding in equilibrium,
Are termed Pradhāna;
In disequilibrium, they are said to be beings.

གཅིག་ལ་རང་བཞིན་གསུམ་ཉིད་ནི། །

དེ་ཡང་སོ་སོར་རྣམ་གསུམ་ཕྱིར། །
[9-128] translation already produced for this document:
For one thing to have three natures
Is illogical, therefore it does not exist.

Because they too would each have three aspects.

heading: ལེའུ་དགུ་པ། ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ།
translation:
That knowledge is also in the world;
Since it exists, why is it not seen?
If the world is not a valid cognition,
Seeing the manifest is also not true.

If valid cognition is not valid,
Is what is measured by it not false?
In reality, emptiness;
Meditating on it therefore becomes untenable.

Without contacting the imputed entity,
Its nonentity is not apprehended.
Therefore, whatever entity is false,
Its nonentity is clearly false.

Work: བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའི་སྤྱོད་པ་ལ་འཇུག་པ།, author: unknown. A canonical Tibetan text; the blocks below are being translated in order.

Preceding blocks of this same document and their translations — match this terminology, register and line shape:

[9-131] source:
སྣམ་སོགས་ལས་ནི་བདེ་སོགས་ཡིན། །
དེ་མེད་ཕྱིར་ན་བདེ་སོགས་མེད། །
བདེ་སོགས་རྟག་པ་ཉིད་དུ་ཡང་། །
ནམ་ཡང་དམིགས་པ་ཡོད་མ་ཡིན། །
[9-131] translation already produced for this document:
Pleasure and so forth are from cloth and so forth;
Since they do not exist, pleasure and so forth do not exist.
Moreover, permanent pleasure and so forth
Are never observed.

[9-132] source:
བདེ་སོགས་གསལ་བ་ཡོད་ཉིད་ན། །
མྱོང་བ་ཅི་ཕྱིར་འཛིན་མ་ཡིན། །
དེ་ཉིད་ཕྲ་མོར་གྱུར་ན་དེ། །
རགས་དང་ཕྲ་བའང་ཇི་ལྟར་ཡིན། །
[9-132] translation already produced for this document:
If the manifestation of pleasure and so forth exists,
Why is the experience not apprehended?
If that itself becomes subtle,
How can it be both coarse and subtle?

[9-133] source:
རགས་པ་དོར་ནས་ཕྲ་གྱུར་པས། །
ཕྲ་རགས་དེ་དག་མི་རྟག་ཉིད། །
དེ་བཞིན་དངོས་པོ་ཐམས་ཅད་ནི། །
མི་རྟག་ཉིད་དུ་ཅིས་མི་འདོད། །
[9-133] translation already produced for this document:
Since it becomes subtle after abandoning coarseness,
That coarseness and subtlety are impermanent.
Likewise, why do you not assert
That all things are impermanent?

[9-134] source:
རགས་པ་བདེ་ལས་གཞན་མིན་ན། །
བདེ་བ་གསལ་བ་མི་རྟག་ཉིད། །
གལ་ཏེ་མེད་པ་འགའ་ཡང་ནི། །
སྐྱེ་མིན་མེད་ཕྱིར་ཞེས་འདོད་ན། །
[9-134] translation already produced for this document:
If coarseness is not other than pleasure,
Manifest pleasure is impermanent.
If you assert that nothing nonexistent
Arises, because it does not exist,

[9-135] source:
གསལ་བ་མེད་པར་སྐྱེ་བར་ནི། །
ཁྱོད་མི་འདོད་ཀྱང་གནས་པ་ཉིད། །
གལ་ཏེ་རྒྱུ་ལ་འབྲས་གནས་ན། །
ཟན་ཟ་མི་གཙང་ཟ་བར་འགྱུར། །
[9-135] translation already produced for this document:
The arising of what is unmanifest
Remains, even though you do not assert it.
If the result abides in the cause,
One who eats food would eat excrement.

[9-136] source:
རས་ཀྱི་རིན་གྱིས་རས་བལ་གྱི། །
ས་བོན་ཉོས་ལ་བགོ་བར་གྱིས། །
འཇིག་རྟེན་རྨོངས་པས་མ་མཐོང་ན། །
དེ་ཉིད་ཤེས་ཀྱིས་བཞག་དེ་ཉིད། །
[9-136] translation already produced for this document:
With the price of a cotton cloth,
Buy a cotton seed and wear it.
If the ignorant world does not see it,
It is established by the knowers of reality.

heading: ལེའུ་དགུ་པ། ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ།
translation:
Whatever, through the proximity of something,
Is seen, and is not when that is absent,
Is artificial and similar to a reflection;
How can there be true existence in that?

translation:
For an entity that exists,
What need is there for a cause?
Yet even if it does not exist,
What need is there for a cause?

བརྟགས་པའི་དངོས་ལ་མ་རེག་པར། །

[9-139] translation already produced for this document:
Without contacting the imputed entity,
Its nonentity is not apprehended.
Therefore, whatever entity is false,
Its nonentity is clearly false.

[9-140] source:
དེས་ན་རྨི་ལམ་བུ་ཤི་ལ། །
དེ་མེད་སྙམ་པའི་རྣམ་རྟོག་ནི། །
དེ་ཡོད་རྣམ་པར་རྟོག་པ་ཡི། །
གེགས་ཡིན་དེ་ཡང་རྫུན་པ་ཡིན། །
[9-140] translation already produced for this document:
Thus, when a child dies in a dream,
The conceptualization thinking, "He does not exist,"
For the conceptualization of his existence
Is the block, and that is also false.

[9-141] source:
དེ་བས་དེ་ལྟར་རྣམ་དཔྱད་པས། །
འགའ་ཡང་རྒྱུ་མེད་ཡོད་མ་ཡིན། །
སོ་སོ་བའམ་འདུས་པ་ཡི། །
རྐྱེན་རྣམས་ལ་ཡང་གནས་མ་ཡིན། །
[9-141] translation already produced for this document:
Therefore, by analyzing in this way,
Nothing whatever exists without a cause.
In individual or assembled
Conditions, it also does not abide.

[9-142] source:
གཞན་ནས་འོངས་པའང་མ་ཡིན་ལ། །
གནས་པ་མ་ཡིན་འགྲོ་མ་ཡིན། །
རྨོངས་པས་བདེན་པར་གང་བྱས་འདི། །
སྒྱུ་མ་ལས་ནི་ཁྱད་ཅི་ཡོད། །
[9-142] translation already produced for this document:
Neither does it come from elsewhere,
Nor does it abide, nor does it go.
This which the ignorant take as true,
What difference does it have from an illusion?

[9-143] source:
སྒྱུ་མས་སྤྲུལ་པ་གང་ཡིན་དང་། །
རྒྱུ་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་ནི་གང་སྤྲུལ་པ། །
དེ་ནི་གང་ནས་འོངས་གྱུར་ཅིང་། །
གང་དུ་འགྲོ་བའང་བརྟག་པར་གྱིས། །
[9-143] translation already produced for this document:
Whatever is emanated by an illusion,
And whatever is emanated by causes,
Where does it come from,
And where does it go? Examine this!

[9-144] source:
གང་ཞིག་གང་ནི་ཉེ་བ་ཡིས། །
མཐོང་གྱུར་དེ་མེད་ན་མིན་པ། །
བཅོས་སུ་གཟུགས་བརྙན་དང་མཚུངས་པ། །
དེ་ལ་བདེན་ཉིད་ཇི་ལྟར་ཡོད། །
[9-144] translation already produced for this document:
Whatever, through the proximity of something,
Is seen, and is not when that is absent,
Is artificial and similar to a reflection;
How can there be true existence in that?

heading: ལེའུ་དགུ་པ། ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ།
translation:
Even by a hundred million causes,
A nonentity cannot be transformed.
How could that state be an entity?
And what else could become an entity?

[9-147] source:
མེད་ཚེ་དངོས་ཡོད་སྲིད་མིན་ན། །
དངོས་པོ་ཡོད་པར་ནམ་ཞིག་འགྱུར། །
དངོས་པོ་སྐྱེས་པར་མ་གྱུར་པར། །
དངོས་མེད་དེ་ནི་འབྲལ་མི་འགྱུར། །
[9-147] translation already produced for this document:
If existence is impossible at the time of nonexistence,
When will it become an existing entity?
Without the entity being produced,
It will not separate from that nonentity.

[9-148] source:
དངོས་མེད་དང་ནི་མ་བྲལ་ན། །
དངོས་པོ་ཡོད་པའི་སྐབས་མི་སྲིད། །
དངོས་པོའང་མེད་པར་འགྱུར་མིན་ཏེ། །
རང་བཞིན་གཉིས་སུ་ཐལ་འགྱུར་ཕྱིར། །
[9-148] translation already produced for this document:
If it does not separate from nonentity,
There is no opportunity for an entity to exist.
An entity also does not become nonexistent,
Because it would follow that it has two natures.

[9-149] source:
དེ་ལྟར་འགག་པ་ཡོད་མིན་ཞིང་། །
དངོས་པོའང་ཡོད་མིན་དེ་ཡི་ཕྱིར། །
འགྲོ་བ་འདི་དག་ཐམས་ཅད་ནི། །
རྟག་ཏུ་མ་སྐྱེས་མ་འགགས་ཉིད། །
[9-149] translation already produced for this document:
Thus, there is no cessation,
And there is no entity; therefore,
All these migrating beings
Are always unproduced and unceased.

[9-150] source:
འགྲོ་བ་རྨི་ལམ་ལྟ་བུ་སྟེ། །
རྣམ་པར་དཔྱད་ན་ཆུ་ཤིང་འདྲ། །
མྱ་ངན་འདས་དང་མ་འདས་པའང་། །
དེ་ཉིད་དུ་ན་ཁྱད་པར་མེད། །
[9-150] translation already produced for this document:
Migrating beings are like a dream;
When analyzed, they are like a plantain tree.
Even passing into nirvana or not passing into nirvana,
In reality, have no difference.

[9-151] source:
དེ་ལྟར་སྟོང་པའི་དངོས་རྣམས་ལ། །
ཐོབ་པ་ཅི་ཡོད་ཤོར་ཅི་ཡོད། །
གང་གིས་རིམ་གྲོ་བྱས་པའམ། །
ཡོངས་སུ་བརྙས་པའང་ཅི་ཞིག་ཡོད། །
[9-151] translation already produced for this document:
Thus, with entities being empty,
What is there to be gained, what is there to be lost?
Who is there to do honor,
Or what is there to completely despise?

[9-152] source:
བདེ་བའང་སྡུག་བསྔལ་གང་ལས་ཡིན། །
མི་དགར་ཅི་ཡོད་དགར་ཅི་ཡོད། །
དེ་ཉིད་དུ་ནི་བཙལ་བྱས་ན། །
གང་ཞིག་སྲེད་ཅིང་གང་ལ་སྲེད། །
[9-152] translation already produced for this document:
From what are happiness and suffering?
What is there to displease, what is there to please?
If searched for in reality,
Who is craving and for what do they crave?

heading: ལེའུ་དགུ་པ། ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ།
translation:
That all things are like space,
May those like me completely grasp.
Those who desire happiness for themselves,
Through causes of conflict and excitement,

heading: ལེའུ་དགུ་པ། ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ།
translation:
Become intensely agitated and elated.
With sorrow, exertion, and disputes,
Cutting and piercing one another,
And through negative deeds, they live in great difficulty.

translation:
Having come again and again to the happy realms,
And having experienced much happiness,
After dying, into the sufferings of the lower realms,
Which are long-lasting and unbearable, they fall.

The appearance of a Buddha is extremely hard to encounter.
The river of afflictions is hard to abandon, so
Alas, suffering will continue in succession.

Work: བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའི་སྤྱོད་པ་ལ་འཇུག་པ།, author: unknown. A canonical Tibetan text; the blocks below are being translated in order.

Preceding blocks of this same document and their translations — match this terminology, register and line shape:

[9-155] source:
རབ་ཏུ་འཁྲུག་དང་དགའ་བར་བྱེད། །
མྱ་ངན་འབད་རྩོལ་རྩོད་པ་དང་། །
ཕན་ཚུན་གཅོད་དང་འབིགས་པ་དང་། །
སྡིག་དག་གིས་ནི་ཚེགས་ཆེན་འཚོ། །
[9-155] translation already produced for this document:
Become intensely agitated and elated.
With sorrow, exertion, and disputes,
Cutting and piercing one another,
And through negative deeds, they live in great difficulty.

[9-156] source:
བདེ་འགྲོར་ཡང་དང་ཡང་འོངས་ཏེ། །
བདེ་བ་མང་པོ་སྤྱད་སྤྱད་ནས། །
ཤི་ནས་ངན་སོང་སྡུག་བསྔལ་ནི། །
ཡུན་རིང་མི་བཟད་རྣམས་སུ་ལྟུང་། །
[9-156] translation already produced for this document:
Having come again and again to the happy realms,
And having experienced much happiness,
After dying, into the sufferings of the lower realms,
Which are long-lasting and unbearable, they fall.

[9-157] source:
སྲིད་པ་ན་ནི་གཡང་ས་མང་། །
དེར་ནི་དེ་ཉིད་མིན་འདི་འདྲ། །
དེར་ཡང་ཕན་ཚུན་འགལ་བས་ན། །
སྲིད་ན་དེ་ཉིད་འདི་འདྲ་མེད། །
[9-157] translation already produced for this document:
In existence, there are many abysses,
And there, reality is not like this.
And because they mutually contradict each other there,
In existence, there is no such reality.

[9-158] source:
དེ་ཡང་དཔེ་མེད་མི་བཟད་པའི། །
སྡུག་བསྔལ་རྒྱ་མཚོ་མཐའ་ལས་འདས། །
དེར་ནི་དེ་ལྟར་སྟོབས་ཆུང་ཞིང་། །
དེར་ནི་ཚེ་ཡང་ཐུང་བ་ཉིད། །
[9-158] translation already produced for this document:
Furthermore, there is the incomparable and unbearable
Boundless ocean of suffering.
There, one thus has little strength,
And there, life is also short.

[9-159] source:
དེར་ཡང་གསོན་དང་ནད་མེད་ཀྱི། །
བྱེད་དང་བཀྲེས་ནའི་ངལ་བ་དང་། །
གཉིད་དང་འཚེ་དང་དེ་བཞིན་དུ། །
བྱིས་དང་འགྲོགས་པ་དོན་མེད་ཀྱིས། །
[9-159] translation already produced for this document:
Even there, for livelihood and health,
Through activities, the weariness of hunger and sickness,
Sleep, harm, and likewise
Meaningless association with fools,

[9-160] source:
ཚེ་ནི་དོན་མེད་མྱུར་འདའ་ཡི། །
རྣམ་དཔྱོད་ཤིན་ཏུ་རྙེད་པར་དཀའ། །
དེར་ཡང་རྣམ་གཡེང་གོམས་པ་ནི། །
བཟློག་པའི་ཐབས་ནི་ག་ལ་ཡོད། །
[9-160] translation already produced for this document:
Life passes quickly and meaninglessly;
Discernment is extremely hard to find.
And there, as for habituation to distraction,
Where is the method to reverse it?

heading: ལེའུ་དགུ་པ། ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ།
translation:
When, in a non-apprehending manner,
Having respectfully gathered the accumulation of merit,
To those who are ruined by apprehension,
Will I teach emptiness?

heading: ལེའུ་བཅུ་པ། བསྔོ་བ།
translation:
To the Conduct of a Bodhisattva,
By my having composed the Entering,
Through whatever virtue that is, may all wandering beings
Enter the bodhisattva conduct.

However many are sick with suffering,
May they, by my merit,
Attain an ocean of happiness and joy.

May they never decline from happiness.

However many there are,
In them, may embodied beings
Rejoice with the happiness of Sukhāvatī.

To those who are ruined by apprehension,

May the rain of embers, burning stones, and weapons
From now on become a rain of flowers.
And may that striking of one another with weapons
From now on become the tossing of flowers for the sake of play.

Their flesh all destroyed, with bones the color of jasmine flowers,
By the power of my virtue attain the bodies of gods,
And abide together with goddesses in the Mandākinī.

Whose noble power is this, that entirely dispels darkness and generates joy and happiness?" Thinking thus,
Looking upward and seeing the blazing Vajrapāṇi residing in the center of the sky,
Freed from negativity through the force of intense joy, may they depart together with him.

Seeing the burning embers of hell sizzling and being extinguished,
And thinking, "What is this sudden satisfaction of happiness?"
May the hell beings see Padmapāṇi.

heading: ལེའུ་བཅུ་པ། བསྔོ་བ།
translation:
"Friends, cast away your fear and come quickly here to us!
By whose power we are freed from all suffering and the force of joy has arrived,
The one who entirely protects all wandering beings, who has given rise to bodhicitta and compassion,
The blazing youth with a topknot who makes us fearless, has arrived!

See how the crowns of hundreds of gods make offerings to his lotus feet,
His eyes moistened with compassion, and a rain of multitudes of flowers falling upon his head,
In delightful tiered palaces containing thousands of goddesses proclaiming songs of praise!"
Seeing Mañjughoṣa like this, may the hell beings now cry out in joy.

And the deaf always hear sounds.
Just as with the goddess Māyā,
May pregnant women give birth without harm.

May those tormented by sorrow obtain joy,
May the despondent be restored in mind,
And may their fortitude be perfect.

May they quickly be freed from illness.
May the diseases of wandering beings, without exception,
Never arise again.

heading: ལེའུ་བཅུ་པ། བསྔོ་བ།
translation:
May the frightened be fearless,
May the bound be freed,
May the powerless become endowed with power,
And may their minds be tender toward one another.

heading: ལེའུ་བཅུ་པ། བསྔོ་བ།
translation:
For all travelers,
May all directions be safe.
Whatever purpose they are traveling for,
May it be accomplished without effort.

"Friends, cast away your fear and come quickly here to us!
By whose power we are freed from all suffering and the force of joy has arrived,
The one who entirely protects all wandering beings, who has given rise to bodhicitta and compassion,
The blazing youth with a topknot who makes us fearless, has arrived!

ཐུགས་རྗེས་བརླན་སྤྱན་དབུ་ལ་མེ་ཏོག་དུ་མའི་ཚོགས་ཀྱིས་ཆར་འབབ་པ། །
ཁང་བརྩེགས་ཡིད་འོང་ལྷ་མོ་སྟོང་ཕྲག་བསྟོད་དབྱངས་སྒྲོགས་ལྡན་འདི་ལྟོས་ཞེས། །
འཇམ་དབྱངས་དེ་འདྲ་མཐོང་ནས་ད་ནི་སེམས་དམྱལ་ཅ་ཅོ་འདོན་པར་ཤོག །

See how the crowns of hundreds of gods make offerings to his lotus feet,
His eyes moistened with compassion, and a rain of multitudes of flowers falling upon his head,
In delightful tiered palaces containing thousands of goddesses proclaiming songs of praise!"
Seeing Mañjughoṣa like this, may the hell beings now cry out in joy.

[10-15] source:
དེ་ལྟར་བདག་གི་དགེ་རྩས་ཀུན་དུ་བཟང་ལ་སོགས། །
བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་སྒྲིབ་པ་མེད་སྤྲིན་བདེ་བ་དང་། །
བསིལ་ཞིང་དྲི་ཞིམ་དང་ལྡན་ཆར་པ་འབེབས་མཐོང་ནས། །
སེམས་ཅན་དམྱལ་བ་དེ་དག་མངོན་པར་དགའ་གྱུར་ཅིག །
[10-15] translation already produced for this document:
Likewise, by my roots of virtue, seeing Samantabhadra and other
Bodhisattvas' unobstructed pleasant clouds,
Letting fall a cool and fragrant rain,
May those sentient beings in hell become truly joyful.

[10-16] source:
དུད་འགྲོ་རྣམས་ནི་གཅིག་ལ་གཅིག །
ཟ་བའི་འཇིགས་དང་བྲལ་བར་ཤོག །

[10-16] translation already produced for this document:
May animals be freed
From the fear of eating one another.
Just like the humans of Uttarakuru,
May the hungry ghosts become happy.

heading: ལེའུ་བཅུ་པ། བསྔོ་བ།
translation:
May those who embark on boats and large ships
Have the wishes in their minds fulfilled,
And having safely reached the shore of the water,
May they rejoice together with their relatives.

ཀུན་ནས་མུན་བསལ་བདེ་དགའ་བསྐྱེད་པའི་མཐུ་བཟང་འདི་ཀོ་སུ་ཡི་མཐུ་སྙམ་སྟེ། །
གྱེན་དུ་བལྟས་ན་ནམ་མཁའི་དཀྱིལ་ན་ཕྱག་ན་རྡོ་རྗེ་འབར་བ་བཞུགས་མཐོང་ནས། །
རབ་ཏུ་དགའ་བའི་ཤུགས་ཀྱིས་སྡིག་དང་བྲལ་ནས་དེ་དང་ལྷན་ཅིག་འགྲོགས་པར་ཤོག །
[10-11] translation already produced for this document:
"Why are the men of Yama, and the unbearable crows and vultures terrified here?
Whose noble power is this, that entirely dispels darkness and generates joy and happiness?" Thinking thus,
Looking upward and seeing the blazing Vajrapāṇi residing in the center of the sky,
Freed from negativity through the force of intense joy, may they depart together with him.

[10-12] source:
མེ་ཏོག་ཆར་པ་སྤོས་ཆུ་དང་འདྲེས་བབས་པ་ཡིས། །
དམྱལ་བའི་མེ་མདག་ཆིལ་ཆིལ་གསོད་པར་མཐོང་གྱུར་ནས། །
གློ་བུར་བདེ་བས་ཚིམ་པ་འདི་ཅི་བསམ་པ་དང་། །
སེམས་དམྱལ་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་ཕྱག་ན་པདྨ་མཐོང་བར་ཤོག །
[10-12] translation already produced for this document:
Through the falling of a rain of flowers mixed with scented water,
Seeing the burning embers of hell sizzling and being extinguished,
And thinking, "What is this sudden satisfaction of happiness?"
May the hell beings see Padmapāṇi.

[10-13] source:
གྲོགས་དག་འཇིགས་པ་བོར་ལ་རིངས་པར་ཚུར་ཤོག་འུ་བུའི་ཐད་དུ་ནི། །
གང་གི་མཐུ་ཡིས་སྡུག་བསྔལ་ཀུན་བྲལ་དགའ་བའི་ཤུགས་ཕྱིན་ལ། །
འགྲོ་བ་ཀུན་ནས་ཡོངས་སྐྱོབ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དང་བརྩེ་བ་སྐྱེས་གྱུར་པ། །
གཞོན་ནུ་ཟུར་ཕུད་ཅན་འབར་འཇིགས་པ་མེད་པར་བྱེད་པ་ཅི་ཞིག་ཕྱིན། །

By whose power we are freed from all suffering and the force of joy has arrived,
The one who entirely protects all wandering beings, who has given rise to bodhicitta and compassion,
The blazing youth with a topknot who makes us fearless, has arrived!

[10-14] source:
ཁྱོད་ཀྱི་ལྷ་བརྒྱའི་ཅོད་པན་དག་གིས་ཞབས་ཀྱི་པདྨ་ལ་མཆོད་ཅིང་། །
ཐུགས་རྗེས་བརླན་སྤྱན་དབུ་ལ་མེ་ཏོག་དུ་མའི་ཚོགས་ཀྱིས་ཆར་འབབ་པ། །
ཁང་བརྩེགས་ཡིད་འོང་ལྷ་མོ་སྟོང་ཕྲག་བསྟོད་དབྱངས་སྒྲོགས་ལྡན་འདི་ལྟོས་ཞེས། །
འཇམ་དབྱངས་དེ་འདྲ་མཐོང་ནས་ད་ནི་སེམས་དམྱལ་ཅ་ཅོ་འདོན་པར་ཤོག །

In delightful tiered palaces containing thousands of goddesses proclaiming songs of praise!"
Seeing Mañjughoṣa like this, may the hell beings now cry out in joy.

དེ་ལྟར་བདག་གི་དགེ་རྩས་ཀུན་དུ་བཟང་ལ་སོགས། །

སེམས་ཅན་དམྱལ་བ་དེ་དག་མངོན་པར་དགའ་གྱུར་ཅིག །

Letting fall a cool and fragrant rain,
May those sentient beings in hell become truly joyful.

དུད་འགྲོ་རྣམས་ནི་གཅིག་ལ་གཅིག །
ཟ་བའི་འཇིགས་དང་བྲལ་བར་ཤོག །

ཡི་དྭགས་རྣམས་ནི་བདེ་བར་གྱུར། །
[10-16] translation already produced for this document:
May animals be freed
From the fear of eating one another.
Just like the humans of Uttarakuru,
May the hungry ghosts become happy.

heading: ལེའུ་བཅུ་པ། བསྔོ་བ།
translation:
May those wandering on astray and dreary paths
Meet with fellow travelers,
And without fear of bandits, tigers, and the like,
May they proceed easily without fatigue.

May those tormented by sorrow obtain joy,
May the despondent be restored in mind,

སེམས་ཅན་ནད་པ་ཇི་སྙེད་པ། །

སྐྲག་པ་རྣམས་ནི་འཇིགས་མེད་ཤོག །

མཐུ་མེད་རྣམས་ནི་མཐུ་ལྡན་ཞིང་། །

May the bound be freed,
May the powerless become endowed with power,

འདྲོན་པ་དག་ནི་ཐམས་ཅད་ལ། །
ཕྱོགས་རྣམས་ཐམས་ཅད་བདེ་བར་ཤོག །
གང་གི་དོན་དུ་འགྲོ་བྱེད་པ། །
དེ་འབད་མི་དགོས་གྲུབ་གྱུར་ཅིག །
[10-23] translation already produced for this document:
For all travelers,
May all directions be safe.
Whatever purpose they are traveling for,
May it be accomplished without effort.

[10-24] source:
གྲུ་དང་གྲུ་ཆེན་ཞུགས་པ་རྣམས། །

མཐུ་མེད་རྣམས་ནི་མཐུ་ལྡན་ཞིང་། །
སེམས་ནི་ཕན་ཚུན་མཉེན་གྱུར་ཅིག །

May the frightened be fearless,
May the bound be freed,
May the powerless become endowed with power,
And may their minds be tender toward one another.

[10-23] source:
འདྲོན་པ་དག་ནི་ཐམས་ཅད་ལ། །
ཕྱོགས་རྣམས་ཐམས་ཅད་བདེ་བར་ཤོག །
གང་གི་དོན་དུ་འགྲོ་བྱེད་པ། །
དེ་འབད་མི་དགོས་གྲུབ་གྱུར་ཅིག །
[10-23] translation already produced for this document:
For all travelers,
May all directions be safe.
Whatever purpose they are traveling for,
May it be accomplished without effort.

[10-24] source:
གྲུ་དང་གྲུ་ཆེན་ཞུགས་པ་རྣམས། །
ཡིད་ལ་བསམ་པ་གྲུབ་གྱུར་ཏེ། །
ཆུ་ཡི་ངོགས་སུ་བདེར་ཕྱིན་ནས། །
གཉེན་དང་ལྷན་ཅིག་དགའ་བར་ཤོག །
[10-24] translation already produced for this document:
May those who embark on boats and large ships
Have the wishes in their minds fulfilled,
And having safely reached the shore of the water,
May they rejoice together with their relatives.

heading: ལེའུ་བཅུ་པ། བསྔོ་བ།
translation:
May all those sentient beings
Have immeasurably long lives.
May they always live happily,
And may even the word "death" not be heard.

Buddhas, and the children of buddhas
Proclaiming the sweet sound of the Dharma,

Be free of gravel and the like,

Freed from all unfree states,
Endowed with faith, wisdom, and compassion,
And perfect in sustenance and conduct,
May they always remember their past lives.

Like the treasury of space,
May their enjoyments be inexhaustible,
And without dispute and without harm,
May they enjoy them independently.

སེམས་ཅན་གཟི་བརྗིད་ཆུང་ངུ་གང་། །

May they become endowed with great splendor.
Whatever ascetics have poor forms,
May they become endowed with perfect, beautiful forms.

May they become men.
May the lowly obtain high status,
And may their pride be subdued.

བདག་གི་བསོད་ནམས་འདི་ཡིས་ནི། །

[10-31] translation already produced for this document:
By this merit of mine,
May all sentient beings without exception
Abandon all harmful deeds
And always perform virtuous ones.

བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དང་མི་འབྲལ་ཞིང་། །
བྱང་ཆུབ་སྤྱོད་ལ་གཞོལ་བ་དང་། །

[10-32] translation already produced for this document:
Never separating from the awakening mind,
And dedicating themselves to the bodhisattva conduct,
May they be fully embraced by the buddhas,
And abandon the actions of Māra.

And may the recitation of secret mantras be accomplished.
May ḍākinīs, rākṣasas, and the like
Be endowed with minds of compassion.

May many bodhisattvas
Adorn the surface of the earth with their excellence,
And remain dwelling there.

Be heard unceasingly.

And may the harvests be perfect.
May kings act in accordance with the Dharma,

And may the recitation of secret mantras be accomplished.
May ḍākinīs, rākṣasas, and the like
Be endowed with minds of compassion.

Recitation, remain well adorned.
May the Saṅgha always be in harmony,
And may the goals of the Saṅgha be accomplished.

And also receive alms.
May their mindstreams be completely pure,
And may they be renowned in all directions.

ངན་སོང་སྡུག་བསྔལ་མི་མྱོང་ཞིང་། །

And without engaging in hardships,

Make offerings to all the buddhas.

May they always be endowed with happiness.

May it all ripen upon me.

Attain solitary places.
Having abandoned all distractions,
May they meditate with pliable minds.

དགེ་སློང་མ་རྣམས་རྙེད་ལྡན་ཞིང་། །

Remain with unblemished discipline.

And may they always exhaust their negative deeds.

The source of all happiness,
May the teaching, along with gain and honor,
Remain for a long time.

[10-51] translation already produced for this document:
And through the kindness of Mañjuśrī,
Until I attain the ground of Perfect Joy,
May I always remember my past lives
And attain ordination.

[10-52] source:
བདག་ནི་ཁ་ཟས་གྱི་ནས་ཀྱང་། །

[10-52] translation already produced for this document:
May I, even with simple food,
Live endowed with vitality.
In all my lifetimes,
May I attain the perfection of solitary places.

[10-53] source:
གང་ཚེ་བལྟ་བར་འདོད་པའམ། །

Whenever I wish to look,
Or even wish to ask a slight question,
May I behold the protector Mañjuśrī himself,
Without any hindrance.

[10-54] source:
ཕྱོགས་བཅུའི་ནམ་མཁའི་མཐས་གཏུགས་པའི། །

As far as the limits of space in the ten directions,
In order to accomplish the aims of all sentient beings,
Just as Mañjuśrī acts,
May my conduct also be like that.

[10-55] source:
ཇི་སྲིད་ནམ་མཁའ་གནས་པ་དང་། །

དེ་སྲིད་བདག་ནི་གནས་གྱུར་ནས། །

[10-55] translation already produced for this document:
As long as space abides,
And as long as beings remain,
So long may I also remain,
To dispel the suffering of beings.

[10-56] source:
འགྲོ་བའི་སྡུག་བསྔལ་གང་ཅིའང་རུང་། །

འགྲོ་བ་བདེ་ལ་སྤྱོད་པར་ཤོག །
[10-56] translation already produced for this document:
Whatever suffering there is for beings,
May it all ripen upon me.
Through the sangha of bodhisattvas,
May beings experience happiness.

translation:
Through whose kindness a virtuous mind arises,
I prostrate to Mañjuśrī.
Through whose kindness I have grown,
I also prostrate to the spiritual friend.

Live endowed with vitality.

And as long as beings remain,
